issues: Out of date: Law No. 58 is no longer in force. Law No. 179 of 31 July 2025 enacted the Digital Code of the Kyrgyz Republic (Code No. 178 of 31 July 2025) and repealed the 2008 law. The Code took effect six months after publication, in February 2026 (ICNL gives 5 February 2026). Personal-data rules now sit in the Digital Code. The note presented the 2008 law as the current regime. Kyrgyz legal databases mark it 'утратил силу' (lost force), and ICNL's February 2026 guidance note confirms the replacement. The dataset's convention is to record replacement in the note (compare ge-2011, ch-1992), so the note is updated.

The DLA Piper page (the only source) is stale on this point. It still says the most recent amendments were made on 29 November 2021 and 12 July 2022, and it does not mention the Digital Code. Its quote remains accurate for the 2008 enactment and in-force dates.

Law title: the official Russian title is 'Об информации персонального характера' ('On Personal Information' / information of a personal nature). The Kyrgyz data-protection agency's English site renders it 'On Personal Information'. 'Law on Personal Data' is DLA Piper's rendering, also used by the unofficial translation on ecoi.net. The law field is adjusted to give the official title with the common rendering in brackets.

Added inForce 2008 (in force 18 April 2008 per DLA; the Jogorku Kenesh adopted it 21 February 2008 and it is dated 14 April 2008). 'Earliest Central Asian law among those checked here' holds within the dataset: the other Central Asian laws are KZ 2013, TJ 2018 and UZ 2019, and there is no Turkmenistan record.
